mainTopic: A daughter's earnings when her brothers support her, who receives her כתובה money, and when the כתובה's lien on the husband's property begins
overview: This amud opens by finishing an answer from the previous page. It then brings רב's ruling that a בת הניזונת מן האחין keeps her own earnings, learned from a פסוק about slaves. The גמרא works out whether רב or שמואל said it, and rules that the הלכה follows רב. A new משנה teaches that a daughter's כתובה money goes to her father if she was only betrothed, but to her if she was fully married. רבי יהודה gives the first כתובה to the father. From the משנה's wording, the גמרא learns that a woman widowed twice may not remarry, following רבי's view that two times make a חזקה. The גמרא first explains רבי יהודה's reason as the father gaining the rights at אירוסין. After רבא's challenge, it corrects this: the כתובה was written while she was under his authority. Finally, רב הונא and רב אסי disagree about when the כתובה's lien on the husband's property begins. רב הונא's ruling about a woman holding two כתובות is shown not to contradict his view.

steps.title: The case is one where he wounded her face
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an answer begun on the previous page. It explains that the case being discussed is one where he injured her in her face.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are dealing with a case where he wounded her in her face.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing an answer from the previous page. It explains the earlier case as one where the girl was wounded in her face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wound on the face lowers her value. That loss of value is a payment that belongs to her father. Reading the case this way settles the earlier challenge without changing the rule being defended.

keyTerms.meaning: In her face, where an injury lowers her value

phrases.english: When he wounded her in her face.
phrases.notes: This is the last line of an answer that started on the previous page. A face wound lowers her value, and that payment goes to her father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from the previous page
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier source seemed to give the father money in a way that challenged the rule
steps.terutzMaskana: The father's money comes from the face wound that lowered her value

steps.title: A daughter supported by her brothers keeps her own earnings
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רב, the גמרא rules that a daughter supported by her brothers keeps what she earns. The source is a פסוק about passing slaves down to sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זירא said in the name of רב מתנה in the name of רב (some say it was רבי זירא): A daughter who is supported by her brothers keeps her earnings for herself. The פסוק says 'you may pass them down to your sons after you.' 'Them' (slaves) you pass down to your sons, but not your daughters to your sons. This teaches that a man cannot pass down to his son the rights he has over his daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב's ruling that a בת הניזונת מן האחין keeps her own earnings. It supports the ruling with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the father was alive, her earnings belonged to him. One might think the brothers inherit that right, especially since they now support her. The פסוק limits what can be passed down to 'them', the slaves, so the father's rights over his daughter do not pass to his sons.

keyTerms.meaning: A daughter who receives her support from her brothers, from their father's estate
Her earnings, the work of her hands

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the one the הלכה later follows (Step 9). Brothers who support their sister do not gain her earnings.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זֵירָא אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: Rav Zeira said that Rav Mattana said that Rav said,
and some say,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Mattana said that Rav said:
A daughter who is supported by the brothers,
her earnings are her own,
as it is written: 'And you may make them an inheritance
for your sons after you.'
'Them' to your sons,
and not your daughters to your sons.
This teaches that a man does not pass down
the right over his daughter to his son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זֵירָא אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ruling on the question of the daughter's earnings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A daughter supported by her brothers keeps her own earnings, because a father cannot pass his rights over his daughter to his sons

steps.title: אבימי בר פפי says שקוד said it
steps.stepSummary: אבימי בר פפי tells רבי זירא that this ruling was said by someone called שקוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבימי בר פפי said to him: שקוד said this.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone comments on who said the ruling. This sets up the next questions about the name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling was just given in the name of רב. Now a different person, שקוד, is named as its author. This creates a puzzle that the next steps work out.

phrases.english: Avimi bar Pappi said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי זירא, who reported the ruling.

phrases.english: Shakud said it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on who said the ruling in Step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling is credited to שקוד

steps.title: Who is שקוד? שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who שקוד is and answers that it is שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is שקוד? שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whom the nickname refers to and answers right away: שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know שקוד is שמואל, a problem appears. Step 2 credited the ruling to רב, not שמואל.

phrases.english: Who is Shakud?
Shmuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the nickname used in Step 3

steps.title: But רב said it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the ruling was given in the name of רב, so how can it be credited to שמואל?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב said it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction. The ruling was reported in רב's name, yet אבימי says שמואל said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain of names in Step 2 ends with רב. Saying that שמואל said it seems to contradict that report.

phrases.english: But Rav said it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 3 using Step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: אבימי's claim that שמואל said the ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling was already reported in רב's name

steps.title: שמואל also said it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that אבימי meant that שמואל said it too, alongside רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: שקוד also said it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by rereading אבימי's words to mean 'שמואל also said it.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both names can be right. רב said the ruling, and אבימי adds that שמואל agrees. This makes the ruling stronger.

phrases.english: Say: even Shakud said it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 5
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אבימי meant that only שמואל said it
steps.terutzMaskana: רב said it, and שמואל agreed

steps.title: נהרדעא rules like רב ששת
steps.stepSummary: מר בר אמימר reports to רב אשי that the scholars of נהרדעא rule like רב ששת.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר אמימר said to רב אשי: The scholars of נהרדעא say the הלכה follows רב ששת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the practical ruling. It reports the view of נהרדעא that the הלכה follows רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת is the one from the earlier discussion who held that the brothers get her earnings. This is the opposite of רב's ruling, so we now have two competing views on the final הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of the city נהרדעא

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר בַּר אַמֵּימָר לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar bar Ameimar said to Rav Ashi:
This is what the Nehardeans say:
The halakha is like Rav Sheshet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בַּר אַמֵּימָר לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the question of how to rule in practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to נהרדעא, the הלכה follows רב ששת

steps.title: רב אשי rules like רב
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי disagrees and says the הלכה follows רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The הלכה follows רב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the opposite ruling: the הלכה follows רב, so the daughter keeps her earnings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up a direct disagreement about the practical ruling. The next line settles it.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב,
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: The halakha is like Rav,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling reported in Step 7

steps.title: Final ruling: like רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the הלכה follows רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final decision: the הלכה follows רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the disagreement between נהרדעא and רב אשי in favor of רב אשי. A daughter supported by her brothers keeps her own earnings.
steps.whatToRemember: A בת הניזונת מן האחין keeps her own earnings. The father's rights over his daughter do not pass to his sons, learned from 'אותם לבניכם'.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two 'הלכתא כוותיה דרב' lines in a row. The first is רב אשי's own opinion; the second is the גמרא's final ruling agreeing with him.

phrases.english: And the halakha is like Rav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between Steps 7 and 8
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב: the daughter keeps her earnings

steps.title: Betrothed only: the כתובה goes to the father
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that if the father betrothed his daughter and she was then divorced or widowed from that betrothal, her כתובה money belongs to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man betroths his daughter and she is divorced, then he betroths her again and she is widowed, her כתובה money belongs to him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that when the daughter was only betrothed (אירוסין) each time, the כתובה money goes to her father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While she is only betrothed, she is still under her father's authority. So money owed to her through her כתובה from these betrothals belongs to him.

keyTerms.meaning: One who betroths (gives her in קידושין)

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who betroths his daughter, and he divorced her,
phrases.notes: 'He divorced her' means the husband divorced her.

phrases.english: he betrothed her again and she was widowed —
her ketuba is his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If she was only betrothed, her כתובה money goes to the father

steps.title: Fully married: the כתובה is hers
steps.stepSummary: If the father married her off (נישואין) and she was divorced, then married again and widowed, the כתובה money belongs to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he married her off and she was divorced, then married her off again and she was widowed, her כתובה money belongs to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case. If she was fully married, the כתובה money is hers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she is fully married, she leaves her father's authority for good. So even the כתובה from her first marriage belongs to her.

phrases.english: If he married her off and he divorced her,
he married her off again and she was widowed —
her ketuba is hers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts full marriage with the betrothal case in Step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After full marriage, her כתובה money is hers

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the first כתובה goes to the father
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the כתובה from the first marriage belongs to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: The first one belongs to the father.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion about the first marriage. He gives that כתובה to the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, the father's right to her first כתובה stays with him even though she was fully married.

keyTerms.meaning: The first one, the first כתובה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The first belongs to the father.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁל אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with Step 11 about the first כתובה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כתובה of the first marriage belongs to the father

steps.title: The Sages answer: after marriage the father has no authority
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה: once the father married her off, he no longer has any authority over her.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Once he has married her off, her father has no authority over her.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back against רבי יהודה. Full marriage ends the father's authority completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their point is that marriage, even the first one, takes her out of her father's control for good. So the first כתובה cannot belong to him.
steps.whatToRemember: Betrothal alone keeps the daughter under her father's authority, so her כתובה money goes to him. Full marriage ends his authority, so the money is hers.

phrases.english: They said to him:
If it is after he married her off,
her father has no authority over her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהודה in Step 12
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי יהודה's claim to the first כתובה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Full marriage already ended the father's authority

steps.title: Why the משנה avoided 'widowed twice'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices the משנה described 'divorced, then widowed' and not 'widowed twice', because a woman widowed twice is not fit to marry again.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason the משנה said 'married off and divorced, married off and widowed' is that a woman widowed twice is no longer fit to marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads a hidden point out of the משנה's choice of words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have said she was widowed twice. It chose a divorce first because, after two husbands die, she is no longer fit to marry. The concern is that she may be the cause of their deaths.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The reason is that he married her off and he divorced her,
he married her off again and she was widowed,
but if she was widowed two times —
she is no longer fit to be married.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a lesson from the wording of Step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman widowed twice may not marry again

steps.title: The משנה quietly follows רבי: two times make a חזקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that, along the way, the משנה's unnamed opinion follows רבי, who holds that a חזקה is set by two times.
steps.simpleTranslation: Along the way, the תנא is teaching us an unnamed ruling that follows רבי, who said that two times create a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what the inference in Step 14 shows. The משנה sides with רבי that two events are enough to set a pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some hold that a pattern needs three events. Because the משנה treats two husbands' deaths as enough, it follows רבי's view that two times create a חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tanna teaches us without naming whose view it is

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's wording shows that a woman widowed twice may not remarry. This follows רבי's view that two times set a חזקה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'רבי' alone here means רבי יהודה הנשיא, not the רבי יהודה who appears in the משנה.

phrases.english: And along the way,
the tanna teaches us an unattributed ruling like Rabbi,
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name after it means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: who said: with two times, it becomes a presumption.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא סָתֵים לַן תַּנָּא כְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general conclusion from Step 14
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's unnamed view follows רבי that two times establish a חזקה

steps.title: What is the reason for רבי יהודה's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's ruling from the משנה and asks for his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the first כתובה belongs to the father. What is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יהודה's words in the משנה and asks why he holds this way. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said that once the father married her off, he has no more authority over her. So it is puzzling that רבי יהודה gives him the first כתובה, since it is only paid after she was married and divorced. The גמרא wants to know what legal basis gives the father this money.

keyTerms.meaning: The first one, meaning the כתובה from the first marriage

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The first belongs to the father.
phrases.notes: This is the line from the משנה we saw in step 12, about the כתובה money from her first marriage.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יהודה's opinion from the משנה to look for its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The legal reason why the father receives the first כתובה even though it is paid after her marriage.

steps.title: The father gained the rights at the time of betrothal
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף explain that the father gained the כתובה rights at the time of אירוסין, when she was still under his authority.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: since the father acquired the rights to the כתובה money from the time of the betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give the same answer: the father's rights started at the אירוסין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the אירוסין the girl was still under her father's authority, and the husband already committed himself to the כתובה then. Even though the money is paid much later, the right to it was already fixed for the father at that earlier moment.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef, who both say:
Since from the time of the betrothal
the father acquired them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The father's rights to the כתובה were set at the אירוסין, while she was under his authority.

steps.title: רבא objects from the case of a girl who grew up before marriage
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה agrees the father gets nothing if the girl became an adult before נישואין. That contradicts the reason of 'from the time of אירוסין'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: רבי יהודה says the first belongs to the father, and he agrees that if a father betroths his daughter while she is a minor, and she grows up and then marries, the father has no authority over her. Why? Here too, let us say the father acquired the rights from the time of betrothal!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the answer of רבה and רב יוסף using a ברייתא about רבי יהודה himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא's case, the אירוסין also happened while she was a קטנה under her father's authority. If the reason were 'the father acquired at אירוסין', he should win here too. Since רבי יהודה says he does not, the reason must be something else.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl who is still a minor
She became a בוגרת, a full adult

steps.confusionAlert: Both cases involve אירוסין while she was a minor. The only difference is that here she became an adult before the נישואין. That difference is what רבא uses to knock down the reason.

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁל אָב.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: The first belongs to the father.
And Rabbi Yehuda agrees
regarding one who betroths his daughter when she is a minor
and she grew up, and afterward she was married,
that her father has no authority over her.
Why?
Here too, let us say:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וּמִשְּׁעַת אֵירוּסִין זָכָה בָּהֶן הָאָב.
phrases.english: Since from the time of the betrothal the father acquired them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason of רבה and רב יוסף that the father acquires at the time of אירוסין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא the אירוסין were also under the father's authority, yet רבי יהודה gives him nothing. So the time of אירוסין cannot be the deciding factor.

steps.title: The corrected reason: the כתובה was written under the father's authority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates what רבה and רב יוסף really said: the father gets the money because the כתובה was written while she was under his authority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said: רבה and רב יוסף both say: since the כתובה amounts are written while she is under his authority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the old version of רבה and רב יוסף's reason and gives a new version that fits the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כתובה is written close to the נישואין. If she was still under her father's authority then (not yet a בוגרת), it was written under his authority and he gets it. If she already grew up before the נישואין, it was written when she was on her own, so the father gets nothing, which fits the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said; the גמרא gives a corrected version of a statement

steps.whatToRemember: Even for רבי יהודה, what counts is when the כתובה is written, close to the נישואין, and not the time of the אירוסין.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said:
Rabba and Rav Yosef both say:
Since they are written under his authority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's objection by restating the reason of רבה and רב יוסף.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrected version of the original statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father's rights come from the time of אירוסין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father's rights come from the כתובה being written while she was under his authority, close to the נישואין.

steps.title: From when can a כתובה be collected?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question: from what point does the כתובה put a lien on the husband's property?
steps.simpleTranslation: And collection: from when does it collect?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question that grows out of the last step. It is setting up a discussion that continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that the writing at the time of נישואין matters for who gets the money. Now the גמרא asks whether the wife can collect from property the husband owned from the אירוסין, or only from property he owned at the נישואין.

phrases.english: And collection,
from when does it collect?
phrases.notes: From which date do the husband's properties count for paying the כתובה: the אירוסין or the נישואין?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion of step 19 to ask a related new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the כתובה's lien on the husband's property starts at the אירוסין or at the נישואין.

steps.title: When the lien begins: רב הונא and רב אסי disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא: the basic כתובה amount puts a lien on the husband's property from אירוסין, and the תוספת only from נישואין. רב אסי: both only from נישואין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: the basic 100 or 200 has a lien from the time of betrothal, and the addition from the time of marriage. רב אסי said: both this and that only from the time of marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two answers to the question from step 20: from when does the כתובה put a lien on the husband's property? רב הונא splits the כתובה into two parts, and רב אסי treats it all the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא says the basic amount (100 for a non-virgin, 200 for a virgin) starts as early as אירוסין, while the extra the husband chose to add only starts at נישואין. רב אסי says nothing starts before נישואין. This matters because the lien date decides which buyers of the husband's land she can collect from.

keyTerms.meaning: 100 זוז, the basic כתובה of a woman who was not a בתולה
200 זוז, the basic כתובה of a בתולה
The extra amount the husband adds to the כתובה on his own
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
A lien: the husband's property is tied to paying the debt

steps.confusionAlert: 'From אירוסין' does not mean she gets paid at אירוסין. It means the lien starts from that date, so land the husband sold after that date can still be taken to pay her.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section tests whether רב הונא really holds that the basic amount and the תוספת can have different starting dates.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The one hundred or two hundred: from the betrothal,
phrases.notes: These are the basic כתובה amounts the חכמים set: 100 for a non-virgin, 200 for a virgin.

phrases.english: and the addition: from the marriage.
And Rav Asi said:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה מִן הַנִּשּׂוּאִין.
phrases.english: Both this and that: from the marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מָנֶה מָאתַיִם מִן הָאֵירוּסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 20 about when the כתובה's lien begins.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא: basic amount from אירוסין, תוספת from נישואין. רב אסי: everything from נישואין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute over whether the basic כתובה amount's lien begins at אירוסין (רב הונא) or only at נישואין (רב אסי).

steps.title: Did רב הונא really say this? His ruling about two כתובות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רב הונא holds this, quoting his ruling that a woman with two כתובות (200 and 300) collects 200 from the first date or 300 from the second date.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב הונא really say this? But it was stated: a woman produced two כתובות against her husband, one of 200 and one of 300. And רב הונא said: if she comes to collect 200, she collects from the first date; if 300, she collects from the second date.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא doubts that רב הונא said this and brings another ruling of his to test it. This step sets up the source; the next step will spell out exactly what the problem is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the woman has two documents written at different times. רב הונא says she picks one: the 200 from the first date, or the 300 from the second date. She cannot mix them, and the גמרא is about to use that to challenge his split between basic amount and תוספת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And did he really say?' — opens a challenge to someone's statement
'But wasn't it stated?' — brings a contradicting teaching of the אמוראים
The first date, when the first כתובה was written

phrases.english: And did Rav Huna really say this?
But wasn't it stated:
She produced against him two כתובות,
one of two hundred,
and one of three hundred.
And Rav Huna said:
If she came to collect two hundred,
she collects from the first date,
phrases.notes: She can take land the husband sold after the first כתובה was written.

phrases.english: if three hundred, she collects from the second date.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַב הוּנָא הָכִי? וְהָאִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's opinion from step 21 using another ruling of his.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that the basic amount's lien starts earlier than the תוספת's.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His ruling on two כתובות forces her to choose one date for the whole amount, which seems not to fit splitting basic amount from addition.

steps.title: The problem spelled out: why not 200 from the first date and 100 from the second?
steps.stepSummary: If רב הונא splits the basic amount from the addition, she should collect 200 from the first date and the extra 100 from the second date.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is so, let her collect 200 from the first date and 100 from the second date.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly why רב הונא's two-כתובות ruling is a problem for his view in step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If different parts of a כתובה can have different starting dates, then the 300 can be split: 200 already had a lien from the first date, and only the extra 100 starts from the second date. But רב הונא made her choose between 200-from-the-first or 300-from-the-second, which looks like he does not allow splitting.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if it is so' — if your claim were true, this should follow
The second date, when the second כתובה was written

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: If רב הונא really lets different parts of the כתובה start on different dates.

phrases.english: let her collect two hundred from the first date,
and one hundred from the second date.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא, תִּיגְבֵּי מָאתַיִם מִזְּמַן רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 22 by stating what should have followed from רב הונא's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's split between the basic amount and the תוספת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the parts can have different dates, she should be allowed to combine: 200 from the first date and the extra 100 from the second. His ruling does not allow this.

steps.title: Pushback: by that logic she should get all 500
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge: if we follow that reasoning, she should collect both documents in full, 200 from the first date and 300 from the second, totaling 500.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, let her collect all 500: 200 from the first date and 300 from the second date!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge from step 23. It shows that the same reasoning would lead to a result nobody accepts, so the challenge proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each document stood on its own, she would collect both, 500 in all, yet רב הונא clearly lets her collect only one. So his ruling about two כתובות is driven by the fact that she can only claim one of them, not by any view about splitting the basic amount from the תוספת. That means it cannot be used to disprove what he said in step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And according to your reasoning' — turns the questioner's logic back on him
Five hundred, the total of both כתובות

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: basic כתובה from אירוסין, תוספת from נישואין; רב אסי: all from נישואין. The challenge from רב הונא's two-כתובות ruling is pushed back, because that same logic would wrongly give her 500.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
let her collect all five hundred?
Two hundred from the first date,
three hundred from the second date!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of step 23 by showing its reasoning leads to an unacceptable result.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using רב הונא's two-כתובות ruling as a proof against his view in step 21.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge's logic proves too much: it would let her collect both documents in full (500), which is clearly not the law.

steps.title: Why can she not collect five hundred?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a woman holding two כתובות (200 and 300) cannot collect both, 500 in total.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is the reason that she cannot collect five hundred?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks the question that Step 24 raised: if each document counted on its own, she would get 500, so why doesn't she?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 showed that the challenge to רב הונא, taken to its end, would give her 500. Since everyone agrees she does not get 500, there must be a reason. Once the גמרא names that reason, it will explain the either/or ruling without hurting רב הונא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces the real question or a new approach

phrases.english: Rather, five hundred:
what is the reason she does not collect it?
phrases.notes: Five hundred is both documents together: 200 from the first plus 300 from the second.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת מַאי טַעְמָא לָא גָּבְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the point made in Step 24 into a direct question about the reason behind the ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The legal reason a woman with two כתובות does not collect both amounts in full.

steps.title: The second document was meant as a choice, not an addition
steps.stepSummary: The husband did not write 'I am adding 300 on top of the 200.' So the second כתובה means: collect 200 from the first date or 300 from the second date. It is a choice, not an addition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he did not write to her, 'I chose to add three hundred for you on top of the two hundred.' This is what he was saying to her: if you collect from the first date, collect two hundred; if you collect from the second date, collect three hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The way the second כתובה was written shows that the husband offered her a choice between the two documents. He did not give her an extra amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Had he written that the 300 was an addition, she would hold two separate debts and could collect both. He wrote a new full document instead, so the גמרא reads it as an either/or offer, and she must pick one. This is why she gets either 200 from the early date or 300 from the later date. That ruling is about reading two documents, so it does not contradict רב הונא's view that the basic כתובה and the תוספת start their liens at different times.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant to tell her
The first date / the second date (the dates written on each document)

steps.whatToRemember: A second כתובה without the words 'I am adding' does not add to the first. It gives the wife a choice: 200 from the first date or 300 from the second. This is how רב הונא's view that the basic amount and the תוספת start their liens at different times survives the challenge.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the second כתובה cancels the first one completely. She can still choose to collect from the first date, but only the 200 written in it.
steps.whyThisMatters: Collecting from the earlier date lets her take back property that was sold after that date. That is why choosing between the dates is worth something, even though it means giving up the extra 100.

phrases.english: Since he did not write to her:
"I chose and I added for you
three hundred on top of the two hundred."
This is what he was saying to her:
If you collect from the first date,
phrases.notes: He means collecting from property that was sold after the date on the first document.

phrases.english: collect two hundred;
if you collect from the second date,
collect three hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא כָּתַב לָהּ צְבֵיתִי וְאוֹסֵיפִית לָךְ תְּלָת מְאָה אַמָּאתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 25. This finishes the defense of רב הונא that began in Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The husband did not write that the 300 was an addition, so the second document is an either/or choice and not an extra debt.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case: the two-document ruling is based on what the husband meant when he wrote the second document, not on when the liens start.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The either/or ruling seemed to show that רב הונא does not split the basic amount from the תוספת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The either/or ruling comes from how the second document was worded, so רב הונא's split between אירוסין and נישואין stands.
